title: Inquest called into RCMP shooting death of hitchhiker
article: The chief medical examiner's office has called an inquest into the death of a man wielding a machete who was shot by an RCMP officer after reportedly stabbing a man while hitchhiking on Dec. 15, 2021.
A Mountie shot Marlon Whincup, 31, in the neck and chest on Highway 16 at Highway 50 near Westbourne, Man., after an 8:50 a.m. call about a stabbing. He was pronounced dead at the scene at 9:44 a.m.

Whincup, who was from Marius near Sandy Bay, repeatedly mounted the hood of a police vehicle and threatened to kill an officer before he was shot, according to a report from the Independent Investigative Unit of Manitoba, which ruled the death a justifiable homicide.
A toxicology report showed "significantly high levels" of methamphetamine and amphetamine in his system, along with a number of other illicit drugs.

RCMP reported a male driver with a female passenger picked up a hitchhiker earlier along Highway 16 and the driver was stabbed without provocation. He was able to pull over and the suspect fled on foot.
The inquest is required in cases of police shootings and will attempt to determine the circumstances related to Whincup's death along with what, if anything, can be done to prevent similar deaths.
The date, time and location of the inquest has yet to be determined.
